name: Five Whys
title: Why 'Five Whys' Almost Never Makes It to Five
subtitle: The first 'why' that names someone else's mistake is exactly where most people stop asking.

substack.email_subject: The ticket has been closed six times this year. Same fix every time.
substack.note:
TICKET-2933 has been closed six times this year. Each time: clear the stuck queue, rerun the batch, mark it resolved. Three to five weeks later, it's back under a new number.

"The queue got stuck" isn't a lie. It's just not the bottom of anything.
steps: Click Copy article below, then paste into the body of a new Substack post.
Copy the Title and Subtitle into their own boxes at the top, then delete the duplicate title and subtitle at the start of the body.
If the image didn't come through, delete the empty space and upload it with the image button (right-click the image above → Save image as…).
Settings → Social preview image: upload the image.
Settings → Email header: paste the email subject line.
Post the Substack Note 1–2 days before you publish.
Click Copy article below, then paste into a new Medium story. The first two lines become the title and subtitle.
If the image didn't come through, click on an empty line, press +, choose the image icon and upload it (right-click the image above → Save image as…).
On the publish screen, add the five tags.
After publishing: ⋯ menu → Story settings → Advanced settings → turn on “originally published elsewhere” and paste the original link.
